identity.description: L2-regularized (by default) linear classifier: models the log-odds as a linear function of features and optimizes penalized log-loss. The transparent classification baseline — every coefficient is a per-unit log-odds effect — and natively near-calibrated because it trains on the proper scoring rule.

axes.note: deterministic under the default lbfgs solver; only saga/liblinear introduce random_state-dependent shuffling

emits.note: trained on log-loss, so probabilities are natively near-calibrated (unlike margin/tree models); multiclass handled via softmax under lbfgs
POINT ESTIMATES ONLY — sklearn computes no standard errors; the enum has no plain 'coefficients' value. For SEs/p-values on a logit, the inference-grade sibling is multinomial_logit (statsmodels)

C.note: INVERSE regularization strength — small C = strong shrinkage

penalty.note: l1/elasticnet require solver saga (l1 also liblinear)

solver.note: chosen by penalty compatibility, not searched

max_iter.note: raise (not search) on ConvergenceWarning; unscaled inputs are the usual culprit

invariances.why: the penalty ‖w‖ is unit-dependent: rescaling a feature rescales its coefficient and therefore its effective shrinkage, so unscaled features are unequally regularized; conditioning of the optimization also degrades
the model is linear in the inputs on the log-odds scale — log/rank/box-cox of a feature changes the fit
the penalized-likelihood solvers have no missing-value path; NaN in the design matrix raises
sklearn requires a numeric design matrix; categoricals must be pre-encoded
assumes the log-odds are LINEAR in the features (Bernoulli likelihood with logit link); a non-linear true boundary is misspecification, not noise
a penalized convex MLE with O(p) parameters is stable from tens of rows per feature; it is the honest choice exactly where boosting overfits
the linear log-odds extend beyond the training range (probabilities saturate toward 0/1 but keep moving monotonically)

featureStats.why: collinearity spreads one signal across correlated coefficients with inflated variance — the per-feature effect story (the Coefficients-class selling point) collapses even when AUC is untouched
imbalance shifts the intercept and hollows out accuracy; flags class_weight='balanced' and PR-AUC/lift as the honest metric

a feature (or combination) that perfectly predicts the class sends the unpenalized MLE coefficient to ±∞ — only the penalty keeps it finite, and its apparent effect size is then set by C, not the data

modelMetrics.why: log-loss training makes probabilities natively near-calibrated; a slope far from 1 flags over-regularization (>1) or overfit (<1) before anyone reaches for a calibrator
one standardized coefficient dwarfing all others is the leakage-dominance signature expressed on the linear scale

edgeCases.behavior: unpenalized MLE diverges; penalized coefficients are finite but scale with C
L2 splits the weight arbitrarily-but-evenly across the copies; per-feature interpretation breaks
coefficients returned from an unconverged solve
edgeCases.note: mitigate by scaling + raising max_iter, not by ignoring the warning

driver.threadSafety: lbfgs fit is single-threaded; predict/predict_proba are thread-safe

canBeSeeds.note: the canonical stacking meta-learner — convex, calibrated, hard to overfit on fold-wise base predictions

placementClaims.why: no native NaN path — the solver raises on missing values
log/Yeo-Johnson of skewed covariates improves the linear-in-log-odds fit the mechanism assumes
the penalty is unit-dependent — unscaled features receive unequal shrinkage and the solver conditioning degrades
categoricals must be design-encoded before the numeric solver sees them
